_note: Inputs to scripts/29_record_corrector.py. Every number here is printed by scripts/28_learned_corrector.py; this file exists so the ledger row and docs/learned_corrector.md quote the same bytes.

anova.notes: scripts/28 --mode anova, 4 local MLPs x 400,000 samples, exact projection onto the layer-1 Hermite family (Mehler Gram, analytic). k=1 reproduces the barrier's f_1 = 0.276 from a fifth independent estimator, so the theorem's constant is right; f_2 ~ 0.16 along the network's own first-layer directions, so the theorem's k=2 instance -- which had never been computed -- is 1/(1-0.43) = 1.75x, not 1.38x. Quoted shares are the plain mean over the 4 MLPs; the per-MLP lists are in the same order as seeds 900000..900003. k>=3 adds ~2% against p/N = 3.0% of estimation noise per block, so k<=2 is the operating point -- a prediction made from this table before the end-to-end run, and confirmed by the unit-coefficient sweep over all 640 generated MLPs (cv1 1.253x, cv1+cv2 1.328x, +cv3 1.197x). raw_final_layer_mse_ref is the sparse-MC baseline over those 640 MLPs, i.e. what the shares are shares OF.

ridge.estimator: corrected_sparse_kernel(tau=2.5, n=8500, P=150, kmax=2) with a 28-feature ridge head, lambda=1e-3, fitted on 384 generated MLPs
ridge.notes: PASSES at 1.516x against a 1.25x bar. The damp=0 ablation runs the identical code path with the head switched off and reproduces the previous ship BITWISE and FLOP-for-FLOP (tests/test_submission_parity.py); it lands on raw 5.8050e-06, the exact number docs/sparse_sign_stable.md published for the shipped file, which is what makes 1.561x raw a same-run comparison rather than a cross-machine one. The head is NOT where the gain is: the mechanism is a layer-1 control variate, exploiting the fact that z^1 = x W^1 is exactly Gaussian so E[He_k(z^1/sigma)] = 0 and Cov(He_k, He_l) = delta_kl k! rho^k are both known in closed form. Two arms ship: an analytic mean-field propagation of the layer-1 mean gap (cv1mf, no estimation noise, biased by the mean-field approximation -- 1.430x alone at unit coefficient over 640 MLPs) and split-sample regression control variates at Hermite orders 1 and 2 (cv1, cv2 -- 1.328x alone). Contracting the regression correction as u = G^-1 d then w_s = u.(g_s - d) collapses it to two length-N matvecs, so the whole feature block is 0.41% of the free budget in FLOPs. The one-pass form of the coefficient estimate leaves a Cov(g'G^-1 g, y)/N self-term that is a bias, not noise, and at k=3 it reverses the sign of the correction; the two-half split fixes it at identical cost. Leave-one-group-out on validation: the Rao-Blackwell/Edgeworth group, the multiplicative-shrink group and the weight/suite-scalar group are each worth EXACTLY 1.000x, which is a direct refutation of the forum's A1 claim that final-layer Rao-Blackwellisation is the dominant win at depth 32. Ablation kept in the shipped design so the table measures the shipped code; it is ~1.3% of the free budget of provable dead weight.

mlp.estimator: one-hidden-layer tanh MLP (16 units) over the same 28 features, full-batch Adam in numpy, 250 epochs
mlp.notes: FAILS at 0.785x against a 1.5x bar -- it is worse than ridge, not merely insufficiently better. Validation 1.328x vs ridge 1.504x; test split 1.063x vs 1.354x. Two learning rates (3e-2, 1e-2) were tried and the better one is reported. The reason is structural rather than a tuning miss: after the control variates the residual is Monte-Carlo noise plus a nearly-linear closure bias, so there is no nonlinear structure for capacity to find, and the extra parameters only fit label noise. This independently reproduces radiant-allomancer's B14 (docs/recon.md: tanh-MLP, GBM and RBF heads all lose to a plain polynomial ridge). Ridge ships; no MLP weights are bundled.
